role: Comms Officer — the voice on the radio
description: A woman, and the voice the party will hear more than any other once they start going out on operations. She works the radio off the plotting floor (data/locations/the-plot-room.json), which means she is reading them the city's picture as it comes in and knows exactly how out of date it is. Unlike the Section Officer, she is on their side: when she tells them to hold back, stay clear, or leave it to someone else, it is because she does not want six trainees killed, not because she is protecting a roster. She has no authority to make them obey and she knows it.
designNotes: Created 2026-09-20 at Ingram's direct request: 'We need a Comms Officer who radios the group. They are an important character who the group will deal with often so they are going to need some nice depth. Make them a woman but apart from that they start as a bit of a blank slate for us to build story around later.' DELIBERATELY UNDER-SPECIFIED -- her history, manner, name and what she wants for herself are all open on purpose, to be built out through play rather than pre-decided here. Her one fixed trait is the care: she warns the party off danger out of genuine fear for them. Her structural job in Episode Two is to be the voice telling them to stay out of the fight -- so that disobeying her is disobeying someone who was trying to protect them, which is a completely different flavour of insubordination than defying the Section Officer. Works out of The Plot Room alongside plot-room-supervisor.json; she is the radio voice, they run the table. Contact designations she reads out come off that plotting floor (see the military-designation convention on the Episode Two encounter).
status: placeholder — not yet named, deliberately a blank slate beyond the care and the radio

facts.text: She will put herself outside procedure to protect somebody and take the consequence herself rather than pass it on. Anybody who knows what a correct transmission sounds like can hear her do it.
She reads every name on the board before a sortie, so she knows theirs before they have met her. Being called by name over a radio by somebody you have never spoken to is her, doing her job.

revealTrigger.narrative: Hearing her use a trainee's own name rather than a section designation.
